answer: Ask the potter what his jar proves and he will point at the wheel, still spinning. Proof of potter jar via wheel turn count is his answer: a jar the potter throws only after 17 turns run even, each turn centred by the potter himself. The onyx is the damp clay the jar is thrown from. The echo is the steady foot that keeps the wheel turning. The cedar is the kiln the jar will fire in. Forging the jar takes 17 turns run even, 17 turns centred true, and a whole afternoon at the wheel, for a jar that still warps in the firing.
